newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Three miners die in accident in Russia's Norilsk.
newsitem.headline: Three miners die in accident in Russia's Norilsk.

text.p: Three miners died in the Russian Arctic town of Norilsk when a bunker collapsed and buried them under ore, a spokesman for the Norilsk Nickel mining group said on Friday.

Sergei Vetchinin said the accident occurred at the company's nickel concentrator plant early on Thursday morning. Rescue crews were brought in but the miners had died by the time they were found on Friday.
"By the middle of Friday it was clear that one person had died," Vetchinin said.

"They tried to save the other two workers (who were buried), but it wasn't possible to remove the ore from above them. They tried to dig a hole from the side. But when they reached the miners they said all three were dead."

Vetchinin said the accident would not have a major impact on production at Norilsk, which aims to become the world's biggest nickel producer this year and is already dominant in palladium and platinum supply, because there were other facilities where losses from one bunker could be made up.

"If a bunker collapses, then of course you have to carry out rescue work and so you can't say it won't affect production at all. But this process does not shake the process of production seriously," Vetchinin said.
"The Norilsk mining region is colossal and every day we have some kind of accident."
Vetchinin said a special commission had been set up to look into the cause of the accident and into ways of avoiding such accidents in the future.
He also said that around 20 people died every year at Norilsk, and so far this year eight lives had been lost.
Norilsk is the town built around Norilsk Nickel's main production complex, called the Norilsk combine. The group has other mining and processing operations in the Kola peninsular near Finland.
